title: Luke Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Luke 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus healed a man with dropsy
Jesus told a parable about choosing the chief rooms
Jesus asked if it was lawful to heal on the sabbath
Jesus instructed to sit in the lowest room at a wedding
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus healed a man with dropsy
questions.explanation: The healing of the man with dropsy is mentioned first in Luke 14:2-4, before the parable and other instructions.

questions.question: Who was watching Jesus as he went into the house to eat on the sabbath day?
questions.correctAnswer: The chief Pharisees
questions.explanation: Luke 14:1 states that Jesus went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, and they watched him.

questions.question: What illness did the man before Jesus have?
questions.correctAnswer: Dropsy
questions.explanation: Luke 14:2 specifies that the man before Jesus had dropsy.

questions.question: What question did Jesus ask the lawyers and Pharisees?
options: Is it lawful to fast on the sabbath day?
Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
Is it lawful to eat bread on the sabbath day?
Is it lawful to forgive sins on the sabbath day?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
questions.explanation: Luke 14:3 records Jesus asking the lawyers and Pharisees if it is lawful to heal on the sabbath day.

questions.question: What did Jesus do to the man with dropsy?
options: He healed him and let him go
He spoke a parable about him
questions.correctAnswer: He healed him and let him go
questions.explanation: Luke 14:4 states that Jesus took the man, healed him, and let him go.

questions.question: What example did Jesus give about pulling an animal out of a pit on the sabbath?
questions.correctAnswer: An ass or an ox
questions.explanation: Luke 14:5 mentions an ass or an ox fallen into a pit as an example Jesus used.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the lawyers and Pharisees to Jesus' question and example about helping on the sabbath?
options: They could not answer him again to these things
They accused him of breaking the law
questions.correctAnswer: They could not answer him again to these things
questions.explanation: Luke 14:6 states that they could not answer Jesus again to these things.

questions.question: What did Jesus observe about those who were bidden to the feast?
options: How they chose out the chief rooms
questions.correctAnswer: How they chose out the chief rooms
questions.explanation: Luke 14:7 says Jesus marked how they chose out the chief rooms.

questions.question: According to Jesus' parable, where should one not sit when bidden to a wedding?
questions.correctAnswer: In the highest room
questions.explanation: Luke 14:8 instructs not to sit down in the highest room when bidden to a wedding.

questions.question: What happens if someone is asked to give place to a more honorable man after sitting in the highest room?
options: They are honored by the host
They begin with shame to take the lowest room
They are asked to leave the feast
questions.correctAnswer: They begin with shame to take the lowest room
questions.explanation: Luke 14:9 states that the person will begin with shame to take the lowest room.

questions.question: Where does Jesus advise one to sit when bidden to a feast?
questions.correctAnswer: In the lowest room
questions.explanation: Luke 14:10 advises to sit down in the lowest room so that the host may invite you higher.

questions.question: Jesus said that whoever exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 14:11 states this principle explicitly.

questions.question: Jesus said to not invite friends, brethren, kinsmen, or rich neighbors to a dinner or supper.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 14:12 specifically instructs not to invite these groups to avoid recompense.

questions.question: Jesus explicitly stated it is lawful to heal on the sabbath day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text shows Jesus asking if it is lawful (Luke 14:3) but does not record Him explicitly stating it is lawful; rather, He heals and challenges their silence.

questions.question: Jesus commanded to always sit in the highest room at a wedding.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 14:8-10 instructs not to sit in the highest room but to choose the lowest room and be invited higher.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Luke 14:13, whom should you invite when you make a feast?
options: The poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind
questions.correctAnswer: The poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind
questions.explanation: Luke 14:13 explicitly commands to call the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind when making a feast.

questions.question: What does Luke 14:14 promise will happen if you invite the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind as commanded in Luke 14:13?
options: You will be praised by men
You shall be blessed and recompensed at the resurrection of the just
You will receive gifts in return
You shall have a great feast
questions.correctAnswer: You shall be blessed and recompensed at the resurrection of the just
questions.explanation: Luke 14:14 promises blessing and recompense at the resurrection of the just for inviting those who cannot repay you, as commanded in Luke 14:13.

questions.question: In Luke 14:16, what action does the certain man take after making a great supper?
options: He sends his servant to invite those who were bidden to come
questions.correctAnswer: He sends his servant to invite those who were bidden to come
questions.explanation: Luke 14:16-17 shows that the man made a great supper and then sent his servant to invite those who were bidden to come.

questions.question: What was the common response of those who were invited to the supper in Luke 14:18-20?
options: They all made excuses for not coming
They invited others in their place
questions.correctAnswer: They all made excuses for not coming
questions.explanation: Luke 14:18-20 records that those invited all with one consent began to make excuses for not attending the supper.

questions.question: What does the master of the house command his servant to do after hearing the excuses of those invited?
options: To invite the rich neighbors instead
To bring in the poor, the maimed, the halt, and the blind from the streets and lanes
questions.correctAnswer: To bring in the poor, the maimed, the halt, and the blind from the streets and lanes
questions.explanation: Luke 14:21 shows the master’s anger and his command to bring in the poor, maimed, halt, and blind after the original guests made excuses.

questions.question: After the servant brought in the poor and maimed, what did the lord say next according to Luke 14:23?
options: To go out into the highways and hedges and compel them to come in
To send for the original guests again
questions.correctAnswer: To go out into the highways and hedges and compel them to come in
questions.explanation: Luke 14:23 quotes the lord commanding the servant to compel others to come in so that his house may be filled.

questions.question: What warning does the lord give about those originally invited to the supper in Luke 14:24?
options: They will be given second chances
They shall taste of the supper
None of those men which were bidden shall taste of the supper
questions.correctAnswer: None of those men which were bidden shall taste of the supper
questions.explanation: Luke 14:24 clearly states that none of those originally invited will taste of the supper due to their refusal.

questions.question: How does Luke 14:15 describe the response of one who heard Jesus' words about the supper?
options: He questioned Jesus about the feast
He said, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God
He made excuses not to come
questions.correctAnswer: He said, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: Luke 14:15 records a man saying that the one who eats bread in the kingdom of God is blessed, showing a hopeful anticipation.

questions.question: What practical lesson about humility is taught in Luke 14:10-11?
options: Always sit in the highest place to show honor
Exalting yourself leads to being abased, and humbling yourself leads to being exalted
Invite only your friends to meals
Do not attend meals on the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Exalting yourself leads to being abased, and humbling yourself leads to being exalted
questions.explanation: Luke 14:11 teaches the principle that those who exalt themselves will be humbled and those who humble themselves will be exalted.

questions.question: Why should one not invite friends, brethren, kinsmen, or rich neighbors to a dinner, according to Luke 14:12?
options: Lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee
Because it is unlawful on the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee
questions.explanation: Luke 14:12 advises against inviting those who can repay you to avoid expecting recompense in return.

questions.question: What reason did the first invited guest give for not attending the supper in Luke 14:18?
options: I have bought a piece of ground and must see it
questions.correctAnswer: I have bought a piece of ground and must see it
questions.explanation: Luke 14:18 records the first excuse given: the man bought land and must go see it.

questions.question: What does the parable in Luke 14 emphasize about responding to God's invitation?
options: Excuses are acceptable reasons not to respond
God desires all to come, and refusal leads to losing the blessing
Only the righteous will be invited
questions.correctAnswer: God desires all to come, and refusal leads to losing the blessing
questions.explanation: The parable in Luke 14:16-24 shows God's invitation extends broadly, but those who refuse lose the blessing of the supper.

questions.question: According to Luke 14:5, what example does Jesus use to illustrate the principle of doing good on the Sabbath?
options: Pulling an ass or ox out of a pit
questions.correctAnswer: Pulling an ass or ox out of a pit
questions.explanation: Luke 14:5 uses the example of pulling an ass or ox out of a pit on the Sabbath to illustrate lawful good deeds.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 14:23, the lord tells the servant to compel people from highways and hedges to come in so that his house may be filled.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 14:23 states the lord's command to compel people from highways and hedges to come in to fill the house.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 14:20 shows that one invited to the supper refused because he was too busy proving five yoke of oxen.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The excuse about proving five yoke of oxen is given in Luke 14:19, not verse 20 which mentions marrying a wife.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 14.

questions.question: According to Luke 14:26, who cannot be a disciple of Jesus?
options: Anyone who does not hate their family
Anyone who does not attend church
questions.correctAnswer: Anyone who does not hate their family
questions.explanation: This is stated in Luke 14:26 where Jesus emphasizes the necessity of prioritizing Him over familial ties.

questions.question: What must one do to be Jesus' disciple according to Luke 14:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Bear his cross
questions.explanation: Luke 14:27 specifies that one must bear their cross and follow Jesus to be His disciple.

questions.question: In Luke 14:28, what analogy does Jesus use to illustrate counting the cost?
questions.correctAnswer: Building a tower
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the analogy of building a tower to illustrate the importance of counting the cost before making a commitment, as stated in Luke 14:28.

questions.question: What happens to the man who begins to build but cannot finish according to Luke 14:29?
questions.correctAnswer: He will be mocked
questions.explanation: Luke 14:29 explains that if a man lays a foundation and cannot finish, onlookers will mock him.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about salt in Luke 14:34?
questions.correctAnswer: Salt is good
questions.explanation: In Luke 14:34, Jesus states that salt is good, implying its value and importance.

questions.question: According to Luke 14:33, what must a person forsake to be Jesus' disciple?
questions.correctAnswer: All that he hath
questions.explanation: Luke 14:33 states that one must forsake all that they have to be Jesus' disciple.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'savour' in Luke 14:34 refer to?
questions.correctAnswer: Taste
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'savour' refers to taste, emphasizing the quality of salt in preserving and enhancing flavor.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Luke 14:26-27?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: In Luke 14:26-27, Jesus uses parallelism to stress the conditions for discipleship by presenting two similar but contrasting statements.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of counting the cost of discipleship in Luke 14:28?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 16:24
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:24 echoes the theme of discipleship, emphasizing the necessity of self-denial and taking up one's cross.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage relates to Jesus' teaching on forsaking all in Luke 14:33?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 19:21
questions.explanation: Matthew 19:21 connects to Luke 14:33 as it highlights Jesus' command to sell possessions and follow Him.

questions.question: What comes directly before Jesus' statement in Luke 14:25?
questions.correctAnswer: He was eating with Pharisees
questions.explanation: Luke 14:1 describes that Jesus was dining with Pharisees, setting the context for the following teachings.

questions.question: In Luke 14:31, what does Jesus say a king must do before going to war?
questions.correctAnswer: Consult his advisors
questions.explanation: According to Luke 14:31, a king must sit down and consult whether he can meet the opposing force before going to war.

questions.question: In Luke 14:30, what do people say about a man who cannot finish building?
questions.correctAnswer: He is foolish
questions.explanation: Luke 14:30 indicates that people will mock the man for being unable to finish, implying he is foolish for not counting the cost.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus emphasizes the importance of family loyalty over following Him in Luke 14:26?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In Luke 14:26, Jesus emphasizes that loyalty to Him must come before family loyalty, not the other way around.

questions.question: Is it false that Jesus teaches about the importance of humility in social settings in Luke 14:10?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 14:10 indeed teaches the importance of humility in social settings, contradicting the statement.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 14:4 teach about Jesus' authority over the Sabbath and healing?
options: Jesus exercises divine authority to heal regardless of Sabbath restrictions
Healing on the Sabbath is forbidden even by Jesus
Jesus defers to Pharisees' understanding of the law fully
The Sabbath law is more important than acts of mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus exercises divine authority to heal regardless of Sabbath restrictions
questions.explanation: Luke 14:4 shows Jesus healing a man on the Sabbath despite Pharisees watching, demonstrating His authority over Sabbath law and prioritizing mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine about humility and exaltation does Luke 14:11 teach?
options: God exalts the humble and humbles the proud
Self-exaltation is the path to divine favor
Exaltation is based on social status
questions.correctAnswer: God exalts the humble and humbles the proud
questions.explanation: Luke 14:11 states that 'whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted,' affirming God's reversal of human pride and humility.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation and recompense does Luke 14:14 teach?
options: Blessing comes from selfless generosity and recompense is in the resurrection of the just
Recompense is guaranteed only by earthly reciprocity
Salvation is earned by inviting only rich and powerful guests
Human generosity is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Blessing comes from selfless generosity and recompense is in the resurrection of the just
questions.explanation: Luke 14:14 teaches that inviting the poor and disabled leads to blessing and recompense at the resurrection, highlighting salvation is tied to selfless love, not earthly reward.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 14:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Luke 14:21, the master commands the servant to bring in the poor and disabled, showing God's sovereign control over His invitation to salvation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 14:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Luke 14:26 emphasizes the radical call to discipleship, which reflects God's holiness demanding total allegiance above earthly ties.

questions.question: How does the parable of the great supper in Luke 14:16-24 connect with the theme of God's kingdom invitation in the Old Testament?
options: It fulfills the prophetic invitation to all nations to partake in God's salvation
It replaces the Old Testament covenant with a purely Jewish feast
It contradicts God's Old Testament promise of exclusive blessing to Israel
It emphasizes human merit as a condition for God’s invitation
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the prophetic invitation to all nations to partake in God's salvation
questions.explanation: Luke 14:16-24 echoes prophetic themes like Isaiah 55:1-3 where God invites all, especially the marginalized, to His banquet, illustrating the kingdom's inclusive invitation.

questions.question: How does Luke 14:33's teaching about forsaking all possessions relate to the broader biblical theme of discipleship?
options: True discipleship requires total renunciation of worldly attachments
Material wealth is a sign of divine favor and discipleship
Possessions have no bearing on spiritual commitment
Forsaking possessions is optional for disciples
questions.correctAnswer: True discipleship requires total renunciation of worldly attachments
questions.explanation: Luke 14:33 states that one must forsake all possessions to be a disciple, aligning with biblical themes that discipleship demands ultimate loyalty to Christ above material things.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 14:28 and Luke 14:31 teach about the nature of discipleship?
options: Discipleship requires careful counting of costs and strategic planning
Discipleship is spontaneous and without need for forethought
Discipleship guarantees earthly success and victory
Discipleship ignores worldly concerns and planning
questions.correctAnswer: Discipleship requires careful counting of costs and strategic planning
questions.explanation: Luke 14:28-31 compares building a tower and going to war to discipleship, teaching that one must count the cost and plan wisely before committing to follow Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 14:7-10 and Luke 14:11 teach about humility and social conduct in the kingdom of God?
options: True honor in God’s kingdom comes through humility and lowliness
Social status guarantees honor before God
Humility is irrelevant to God’s kingdom
One should seek the highest places to ensure God’s favor
questions.correctAnswer: True honor in God’s kingdom comes through humility and lowliness
questions.explanation: Luke 14:7-10 and 14:11 teach that humility in social conduct leads to exaltation by God, opposing worldly ambition for status.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 14:12-14 and Luke 14:21-24 teach about the nature of God's invitation and human response?
options: God’s invitation extends primarily to the marginalized, but many reject it with excuses
God’s invitation is limited to the wealthy and influential
Human response to God’s invitation is always enthusiastic
The invitation to God’s feast is only symbolic and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God’s invitation extends primarily to the marginalized, but many reject it with excuses
questions.explanation: Luke 14:12-14 and 21-24 show God inviting the poor and disabled, but many initially invited make excuses, illustrating the rejection of God’s kingdom offer by many.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Luke 14:25-27 teaches that hating one’s family is a moral imperative. What does Luke 14:25-27 actually teach?
options: Radical allegiance to Christ must surpass all earthly ties, not literal hatred
Jesus commands literal hatred and rejection of family
Discipleship is optional and does not require sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Radical allegiance to Christ must surpass all earthly ties, not literal hatred
questions.explanation: Luke 14:25-27 uses strong language to emphasize that loyalty to Christ must come before family and self, not advocating literal hatred but prioritizing discipleship.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 14:34 teach about the role and condition of believers in the world?
options: Believers must maintain their 'saltiness' to be effective witnesses
Salt losing its savor symbolizes believers losing wealth
Salt is irrelevant to believers’ spiritual witness
Believers are to separate themselves completely from the world
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must maintain their 'saltiness' to be effective witnesses
questions.explanation: Luke 14:34 uses salt as a metaphor for believers’ influence; losing savor means losing effectiveness in witnessing and sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated in Luke 14:23 by sending servants to compel the marginalized to come in?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Luke 14:23 shows God’s mercy in persistently inviting the marginalized to His banquet, demonstrating His gracious outreach to the rejected.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Luke 14:5 contribute to regarding Jesus' fulfillment of the Law and Prophets?
options: Jesus reinterprets the Law by prioritizing mercy over ritualistic Sabbath observance
Jesus insists on strict legalistic observance of Sabbath
Jesus ignores the Law in His ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus reinterprets the Law by prioritizing mercy over ritualistic Sabbath observance
questions.explanation: Luke 14:5 uses the example of rescuing an ox on the Sabbath to argue that acts of mercy fulfill the Law’s intent, showing Jesus’ fulfillment of the Law and Prophets.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 14:27 and Luke 14:33 teach about the cost and nature of true discipleship?
options: True discipleship requires self-denial and forsaking all possessions
Discipleship can be pursued without sacrifice
Carrying the cross is metaphorical for social status
Possessions and family ties are irrelevant to discipleship
questions.correctAnswer: True discipleship requires self-denial and forsaking all possessions
questions.explanation: Luke 14:27 and 14:33 emphasize that bearing one’s cross and forsaking all possessions are necessary for discipleship, highlighting costly commitment.
